101.solution: For \(n=100\) tosses, \(P(\text{even number of heads}) = \sum_{k \text{ even}} \binom{100}{k}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{100}\).\nUsing \((1+1)^{100} + (1-1)^{100} = 2\sum_{k\text{ even}}\binom{100}{k}\), the sum of even-index binomial coefficients \(= \frac{2^{100}+0}{2} = 2^{99}\).\n\(\therefore P = \frac{2^{99}}{2^{100}} = \frac{1}{2}\).

102.solution: Using the identity \((\overline{a}\times\overline{b})\cdot(\overline{c}\times\overline{d}) = (\overline{a}\cdot\overline{c})(\overline{b}\cdot\overline{d}) - (\overline{a}\cdot\overline{d})(\overline{b}\cdot\overline{c})\), the given determinant equals \((\overline{a}\times\overline{b})\cdot(\overline{c}\times\overline{d}) = 0\).\n\(\therefore (2\widehat{i}+3\widehat{j}-\widehat{k})\cdot(3\widehat{i}+2\widehat{j}+\lambda\widehat{k}) = 0\)\n\(\Rightarrow 6+6-\lambda = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = 12\).

103.subtopic: Properties of Triangles — Sine/Cosine Rules and Projection
103.solution: Using the half-angle formula \(\cos\frac{B}{2} = \sqrt{\frac{s(s-b)}{ca}}\) and equating to \(\sqrt{\frac{c+a}{2a}}\):\n\(\frac{c+a}{2a} = \frac{s(s-b)}{ca} = \frac{(a+c)^2 - b^2}{4ac}\).\nCross-multiplying: \(2c(c+a) = a^2 + 2ac + c^2 - b^2\), giving \(a^2 = b^2 + c^2\).

104.subtopic: Combined Equation and Condition for Pair of Lines
104.solution:
Bisectors of the coordinate axes have slopes \(1\) and \(-1\).
Line through \((-2,3)\) with slope \(1\): \(x-y+5=0\).
Line through \((-2,3)\) with slope \(-1\): \(x+y-1=0\).
Joint equation: \((x-y+5)(x+y-1) = x^2 - y^2 + 4x + 6y - 5 = 0\).

105.subtopic: Equation of Circle from Diameter, Centre, and Concentric Conditions
105.solution: Radius \(= OA = \sqrt{2^2+4^2} = 2\sqrt{5}\), the circumradius of the equilateral triangle.\nFor an equilateral triangle the median = altitude, and circumradius \(R = \frac{2}{3}\) of the median.\n\(\therefore\) median \(= \frac{3}{2}R = \frac{3}{2}(2\sqrt{5}) = 3\sqrt{5}\) units.

107.solution: Line through \((1,2)\) parallel to \(3x-y=2\) is \(3x-y-1=0\).\nIts intersection with \(x+y=0\) is \(\left(\frac{1}{4},-\frac{1}{4}\right)\).\nDistance \(= \sqrt{\left(1-\frac{1}{4}\right)^2 + \left(2+\frac{1}{4}\right)^2} = \sqrt{\frac{9}{16}+\frac{81}{16}} = \frac{3\sqrt{10}}{4}\) units.

112.solution: Sum of probabilities: \(\frac14+K+\frac14+\frac13 = 1 \Rightarrow K=\frac16\).\n\(\mu = -3(\tfrac14)+0+1(\tfrac14)+\alpha(\tfrac13) = \frac{\alpha}{3}-\frac12\).\nUsing \(\sigma-\mu=2\) and \(\sigma^2 = E(X^2)-\mu^2\), solving gives \(\alpha=6\), \(\mu=\frac32\), so \(\sigma = 2+\mu = \frac72\).

113.solution: \(P(\text{win}) = \frac13\), \(P(\text{lose}) = \frac23\). Net gains: \(+40\) on win, \(-20\) per losing throw.\n\(E = 40(\tfrac13) + 20(\tfrac23)(\tfrac13) + 0(\tfrac23)^2(\tfrac13)\cdots\), computing the four cases (win 1st: +40; lose-win: +20; lose-lose-win: 0; lose all 3: \(-60\)):\n\(E = 40(\tfrac13)+20(\tfrac29)+0(\tfrac{4}{27})+(-60)(\tfrac{8}{27}) = \frac{360+120-480}{27} = 0\).

114.solution: Newton's law: \(\log(T-290) = -kt + c\). At \(t=0\), \(T=370\Rightarrow c=\log 80\).\nAt \(t=10\), \(T=330\Rightarrow \log 40 = -10k+\log 80\Rightarrow k = \frac{1}{10}\log 2\).\nAt \(T=295\): \(\log 5 = -\frac{t}{10}\log 2 + \log 80 \Rightarrow \frac{t}{10}\log 2 = \log 16\Rightarrow t = 40\) min.

115.solution: Equation is homogeneous: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{y}{x}\left[\log\frac{y}{x}+1\right]\).\nPut \(v=\frac{y}{x}\): \(v+x\frac{dv}{dx} = v(\log v+1)\Rightarrow x\frac{dv}{dx}=v\log v\Rightarrow \frac{dv}{v\log v} = \frac{dx}{x}\).\nIntegrating: \(\log(\log v) = \log x + \log c \Rightarrow \log v = cx\Rightarrow \log\frac{y}{x} = cx\).

116.subtopic: Order, Degree, Formation of ODE, and Verification of Solutions
116.solution: \(\sqrt{\frac{dy}{dx}} = 4\frac{dy}{dx}+7x\). Squaring removes the radical, giving \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 16\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + 56x\frac{dy}{dx}+49x^2\).\nHighest derivative is the first order, raised to power \(2\): order \(=1\), degree \(=2\).

117.subtopic: Order, Degree, Formation of ODE, and Verification of Solutions
117.solution: Circle touching Y-axis at origin with centre \((h,0)\): \(x^2+y^2 = 2hx\), i.e. \(x^2-2hx+y^2=0\).\nDifferentiating: \(2x-2h+2y\frac{dy}{dx}=0\Rightarrow h = x+y\frac{dy}{dx}\).\nSubstituting back: \(x^2 - 2x\left(x+y\frac{dy}{dx}\right)+y^2 = 0 \Rightarrow x^2 - y^2 + 2xy\frac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

118.subtopic: Area Bounded by Curves, Axes, and Lines
118.solution: Intersection of \(x^2=8y\) and \(x-8y+2=0\): points \(\left(-1,\frac18\right)\) and \(\left(2,\frac12\right)\).\nArea \(= \int_{-1}^{2}\left(\frac{2+x}{8} - \frac{x^2}{8}\right)dx = \frac{1}{8}\left[2x+\frac{x^2}{2}-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-1}^{2} = \frac{9}{16}\) sq. units.

128.solution: \(4y^2-4y+2x-1=0\). Tangent parallel to Y-axis \(\Rightarrow \frac{dx}{dy}=0\).\nDifferentiating w.r.t. \(y\): \(8y-4+2\frac{dx}{dy}=0\Rightarrow \frac{dx}{dy}=2-4y=0\Rightarrow y=\frac12\).\nSubstituting: \(1-2+2x-1=0\Rightarrow x=1\). Point \(\left(1,\frac12\right)\).

130.solution: \(\tan\frac{A-B}{2} = \frac{a-b}{a+b}\cot\frac{C}{2}\). With \(a=5,b=4\): \(\frac{a-b}{a+b}=\frac19\).\n\(\cos(A-B)=\frac{31}{32}\Rightarrow \tan\frac{A-B}{2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{63}}\), so \(\frac19\cot\frac{C}{2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{63}}\Rightarrow \tan\frac{C}{2}=\frac{\sqrt7}{3}\).\n\(\cos C = \frac{1-7/9}{1+7/9} = \frac18\). By cosine rule \(c^2 = 25+16-40(\tfrac18) = 36\Rightarrow c=6\).

131.solution: Statement: \(\forall M>0,\ \exists x\in S\) such that \(x\ge M\).\nNegation flips quantifiers and the inequality: \(\exists M>0\) such that \(\forall x\in S,\ x<M\).

141.solution: Line QR: \(\frac{x-3}{-1}=\frac{y+4}{1}=\frac{z+5}{6}=\lambda\), point \((3-\lambda,\lambda-4,6\lambda-5)\).\nOn plane \(2x+y+z=7\): \(2(3-\lambda)+\lambda-4+6\lambda-5=7\Rightarrow 5\lambda=10\Rightarrow\lambda=2\), point \(M(1,-2,7)\).\n\(PM = \sqrt{(1-3)^2+(-2-4)^2+(7-4)^2} = \sqrt{4+36+9} = 7\) units.

Around a round table with the alternating constraint, the seating frame is fixed once the block's position and the alternation are set.\nThe 4 girls fill girl-seats in \(4!\) ways and 4 boys fill boy-seats in \(4!\) ways: total \(= 4!\times 4! = 576\).

144.solution: \(2(\overline{a}\times\overline{b}) = 3(\overline{c}\times\overline{a})\Rightarrow \overline{a}\times(2\overline{b}+3\overline{c})=0\Rightarrow \overline{a}=\lambda(2\overline{b}+3\overline{c})\).\nWith \(|\overline{b}|=\tfrac12,|\overline{c}|=2\), \(\overline{b}\cdot\overline{c}=\tfrac12\cdot2\cdot\cos\tfrac{2\pi}{3}=-\tfrac12\): \(|2\overline{b}+3\overline{c}|^2 = 4(\tfrac14)+9(4)+12(-\tfrac12)=31\), so \(\lambda^2=1\).\nThen \(\left|\frac{\overline{a}\times\overline{c}}{\overline{a}\cdot\overline{b}}\right|^2\): with \(\overline{a}=2\overline{b}+3\overline{c}\), \(\overline{a}\times\overline{c}=2(\overline{b}\times\overline{c})\) and \(\overline{a}\cdot\overline{b}=2|\overline{b}|^2+3\overline{b}\cdot\overline{c}=\tfrac12-\tfrac32=-1\); \(|\overline{b}\times\overline{c}|=\tfrac12\cdot2\cdot\sin\tfrac{2\pi}{3}=\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\), so \(|\overline{a}\times\overline{c}|=\sqrt3\). Ratio squared \(= \frac{3}{1}=3\).
